A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EARL-BO and retain matching methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including v2's new Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on four synthetic functions and three HPO-B search spaces, together with learning-rate, sparse-data, and training-convergence analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds 30-dimensional benchmarks, encoder and horizon ablations, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The Attention-DeepSets encoder, PPO objectives, GP virtual environment, TuRBO initialization, layer freezing, and fallback procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 preserves the procedure. Describing the framework as modular and Dyna-style, with optional alternative components, does not establish a changed implemented method.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 adds 30-dimensional versions of Ackley, Levy, Rosenbrock, and Sum Squares beyond v1's 2-D, 5-D, and 8-D synthetic coverage. This substantially extends the dimensional conditions tested. The three HPO-B search spaces remain unchanged.

E2.justification: SAASBO is newly evaluated in the retained synthetic and HPO comparisons, as confirmed by Figure 2 and v2's Figure 4. Conversely, Figure A2 removes the TuRBO comparator present in v1's sparse-initialization experiment. The existing UCB, EI, PI, and EARL-BO curves remain there.

E3.justification: Retained benchmark ranges, initialization sizes, regret metric, and Table 1 hyperparameters remain unchanged. New analyses introduce an attention-only control, additional one- and seven-step horizons, and a timing protocol specifying 1000 Monte Carlo iterations and a 3600-second timeout for rollout.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds an Attention-DeepSets versus attention-only comparison at two horizons and extends horizon analysis to 1, 3, 5, and 7 steps. New Appendix C examines computational overhead and dimensional scaling. The earlier learning-rate, sparse-data, and training-convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Figure 2's lines as ten-run means and its shading as one standard deviation. v1 already reports ten repetitions and discusses standard deviations, but does not specify this band convention there. This is a reporting clarification, not evidence of increased replication.

E6.justification: New results show EARL-BO leading all four 30-D comparisons, while added SAASBO results outperform it on lower-dimensional Sum Squares. Figures A5–A6 add encoder and horizon findings. Table 2 reports 840 ± 147 seconds for three-step EARL-BO versus rollout exceeding 3600 seconds. Figure A2 removes TuRBO's result.

T1.justification: The GP equations, MDP formulation, reward definition, encoder equations, PPO losses, and parameter-freezing expressions retain their mathematical substance. Renumbering and notation cleanup introduce no new derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of scalable, non-myopic RL-based BO and improved optimization performance remain. v2 broadens the contribution framing toward a modular framework accommodating alternative encoders, RL algorithms, and initialization methods, while explicitly characterizing its learning as model-based.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of SAASBO's advantages on additive, unimodal functions, interprets the new dimensional and encoder results, and discusses when computational overhead is justified by expensive function evaluations. These substantially expand applicability and tradeoff discussion; the earlier planning-delusion explanation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds per-iteration computational requirements, rollout timeout and Monte Carlo settings, and approximately 1600-second runtime information for 30-D Ackley. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, fallback details, and baseline access links are largely retained. Implementation details for the newly evaluated SAASBO baseline are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds a Learning to Optimize subsection discussing RIBBO, POM, and broader L2O research, expands coverage to SAASBO, and positions EARL-BO within model-based RL and Dyna-style learning. Additional acquisition-optimization and dataset-encoding references further expand its relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The principal section sequence and much existing exposition remain. Focused rewrites shorten the abstract, clarify modular and model-based terminology, and expand the algorithm explanation. A new L2O subsection, computational-cost appendix, and impact statement extend the existing structure without wholesale reorganization.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial figure and algorithm resizing. Figure 2 gains consolidated legends, new Figure 3 and Figures A5–A6 are added, and Table 2 presents runtimes. Figure A2 changes from logarithmic to linear scaling; the HPO figure moves from Figure 3 to Figure 4.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for v1's scalability and architectural claims through 30-D benchmarks, SAASBO comparisons, encoder and horizon ablations, and explicit runtime analysis. These additions make both effectiveness and computational tradeoffs more assessable. Missing SAASBO implementation details and removal of TuRBO from Figure A2 limit the revision, but the overall gain in empirical support and practical transparency is substantial.
